title: Tokenisation is not in APX
why_read: Proving that tokenisation is not in APX — meaning no polynomial-time algorithm can even approximate the optimal solution within a constant factor — is a sharp theoretical result with direct implications for every NLP practitioner relying on BPE or unigram tokenisers.
analysis: Tokenisation turns raw text into a vocabulary of subword units, and this paper proves that finding the best tokeniser is not just NP-hard but APX-hard. APX-hardness means no efficient algorithm can guarantee a solution within any fixed percentage of optimal, ruling out a whole class of approximation approaches. This holds for the two most common objectives — compression rate and unigram log-likelihood — and for both the BPE-style and unigram-style tokenisation algorithms used in practice. The result is theoretically clean and has real practical weight: it explains why tokenisation heuristics behave unpredictably and suggests that the field may be optimising an inherently intractable objective.
